title: Nested and Recursive Object Types knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to use a type or build feature?
options: Assume compiler configuration has identical behavior in every version.

Treat type-level examples as proof of runtime correctness.
Choose the feature that expresses the contract, check compiler diagnostics, and verify the configured tool/runtime behavior.
questions.answer_key: Choose the feature that expresses the contract, check compiler diagnostics, and verify the configured tool/runtime behavior.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Nested and Recursive Object Types”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.

questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with nested application data and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Nested application data”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Nested and Recursive Object Types”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check recursive tree-like structures, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume modeling hierarchical data safely is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check recursive tree-like structures, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Recursive tree-like structures”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
